author_or_institution: U.S. Department of the Treasury / Federal Insurance Office
title: U.S. Department of the Treasury Report: Homeowners Insurance Costs Rising, Availability Declining as Climate-Related Events Take Their Toll
book_use: Nationwide homeowners-insurance analysis covering more than 246 million policy-years; higher costs and reduced availability in higher-risk areas.; Chapter: 1;6;7;8;17; Caveat: Data cover 2018-2022 and are aggregated to ZIP Code level; not a 2026 market snapshot.

title: Report on the Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 — Housing
book_use: Six percent of homeowners reported no homeowners insurance; affordability and lack of insurer availability were reported reasons.; Chapter: 1;6;17; Caveat: Self-reported survey data; does not establish causation for any individual market.

title: Key Statistics & Data
book_use: As of June 2026 the FAIR Plan reported $768 billion of exposure and 696,562 dwelling and commercial policies in force.; Chapter: 1;7;8;9;19; Caveat: Exposure is insured value, not probable catastrophe loss; FAIR Plan is an interested market participant.

title: Global natural catastrophe losses in 2025
book_use: Swiss Re estimated $107 billion of global insured natural-catastrophe losses in 2025, including about $40 billion from Los Angeles wildfires and more than $50 billion from severe convective storms.; Chapter: 7;10;11;18;20;21; Caveat: Industry loss estimates can be revised; event attribution and insured-loss estimates are not forecasts of future years.

title: Sustainable Insurance Strategy
book_use: California links forward-looking catastrophe models and recognition of reinsurance costs to enforceable commitments to write more policies in wildfire-distressed areas.; Chapter: 8;17;20; Caveat: California-specific regulatory structure; the Department is describing its own reform program.

title: 2026 Operating Budget
book_use: Citizens described major 2025 depopulation and projected a sharp reduction in policies in force as private-market capacity improved.; Chapter: 8;9; Caveat: Citizens is an interested residual-market institution; projected counts can differ from realized counts.

title: High-Risk Series: National Flood Insurance Program
book_use: As of February 2025 FEMA owed Treasury $22.5 billion for NFIP even after $16 billion of debt cancellation in 2017; GAO calls for comprehensive reform.; Chapter: 9;17;19; Caveat: GAO analysis concerns federal fiscal exposure, not a claim that every NFIP policy is underpriced.

title: Flood Insurance: FEMA's New Rate-Setting Methodology Improves Actuarial Soundness but Highlights Need for Broader Program Reform
book_use: Risk Rating 2.0 more closely aligns premiums with property-level flood risk while affordability and broader program design remain unresolved.; Chapter: 9;17; Caveat: Predates later NFIP changes; use for design logic rather than current premium levels.

title: National Flood Insurance Program — community and floodplain management guidance
book_use: NFIP participation ties access to flood insurance to community floodplain-management responsibilities and mitigation requirements.; Chapter: 9;20; Caveat: Program details can change; this guidance should not substitute for current local ordinances.

title: Terrorism Risk Insurance Program
book_use: TRIA created a shared public-private compensation framework for certified terrorism losses and is authorized through 2027.; Chapter: 9;19; Caveat: Terrorism backstop design is not automatically transferable to cyber, pandemic, climate or AI.

title: TRIP Reports and Resources
book_use: Treasury continues to assess effectiveness and market participation under TRIP, including a June 2026 effectiveness report.; Chapter: 19;21; Caveat: Program evidence concerns terrorism insurance; broader backstop analogies are the author's.

title: Pandemic Risk: Federal Insurance Approaches Would Entail Costs to Taxpayers and Businesses Might Not Participate
book_use: GAO found private insurance played a limited role in pandemic business losses and modeled federal approaches in which government would assume most or all of the risk.; Chapter: 5;19;21; Caveat: Pandemic correlation differs from cyber, AI and natural catastrophe correlation.

title: Insurance Topics: Artificial Intelligence
book_use: NAIC documents state-regulatory work on insurer use of AI, including the 2023 Model Bulletin and third-party model oversight.; Chapter: 13;21; Caveat: NAIC materials coordinate state regulation but are not themselves uniform binding law in every state.

title: NAIC Members Approve Model Bulletin on Use of AI by Insurers
book_use: The Model Bulletin sets governance, risk-management, testing and documentation expectations and reminds insurers that AI-supported decisions remain subject to existing insurance law.; Chapter: 13; Caveat: A bulletin is not a model law or regulation and adoption varies by state.

author_or_institution: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
title: Financial Stability Report — December 2025
book_use: EIOPA identifies potential AI-related channels including common-model correlated behaviour, third-party dependencies, granular-segmentation demutualisation pressures and emerging AI-risk insurance markets.; Chapter: 12;13;14;21; Caveat: European prudential analysis; scenarios and channels are not claims that systemic failure has already occurred.

author_or_institution: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
title: Insurance Risk Dashboard
book_use: July 2026 dashboard raised digitalisation and cyber risk to high, citing frontier AI, geopolitics and elevated cyber underwriting exposure.; Chapter: 12;13;21; Caveat: Dashboard is an assessment framework, not a prediction of insured loss.

title: ILS market insights: February 2026
book_use: Swiss Re reported record 2025 ILS issuance of $24.7 billion and outstanding notional near $60 billion.; Chapter: 10;11;18;21; Caveat: Issuer/intermediary market source; figures describe notional issuance, not expected catastrophe loss.

title: ILS market insights: July 2026
book_use: Catastrophe-bond issuance exceeded $17 billion across 64 transactions in the first half of 2026, the strongest first half on record according to Swiss Re.; Chapter: 11;21; Caveat: Market data from an active participant; issuance volume does not by itself prove cheaper protection.

title: PBGC releases FY 2025 Annual Report
book_use: PBGC reported a fifth consecutive year in which both single-employer and multiemployer insurance programs had positive net financial positions.; Chapter: 16;19; Caveat: Positive net position does not remove long-term policy, demographic or sponsor risks.

title: Private Health Insurance: Market Concentration Generally Increased from 2011 through 2022
book_use: GAO found three or fewer insurers held at least 80% of individual and employer-group market enrollment in at least 35 states.; Chapter: 15; Caveat: Enrollment concentration is not by itself proof of anticompetitive conduct or the sole cause of premiums.

title: Insurance Topics: Long-Term Care Insurance
book_use: NAIC explains that older LTC blocks were often priced with immature experience; claim incidence/duration were understated and lapse rates lower than assumed, contributing to later rate increases.; Chapter: 15;16; Caveat: General market history; individual policy blocks differ.

title: History — Coffee and Commerce
book_use: Lloyd's documents the late-seventeenth-century coffeehouse's role as a center of shipping information and marine underwriting and the later subscription market.; Chapter: 3; Caveat: Lloyd's own institutional history; marine insurance predates Lloyd's and developed in multiple commercial centers.

title: FM History — From 1835 Innovation to Global Resilience Leadership
book_use: FM traces the Factory Mutual tradition to Zachariah Allen's loss-prevention approach and the use of engineering and inspections to reduce property loss.; Chapter: 3;20; Caveat: FM's account of its own lineage; use for institutional history, not neutral comparative evidence.

title: Actuarial Standard of Practice No. 12: Risk Classification
book_use: ASOP 12 defines risk classification, adverse selection, credibility and the balance between homogeneity and practical/credible classes.; Chapter: 2;4;13;17; Caveat: Professional guidance, not a social-policy rule about which classifications should be legal or fair.

title: Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program
book_use: World Bank describes sovereign disaster-risk finance as a way to increase post-disaster funding capacity without compromising fiscal balance and development objectives.; Chapter: 18;19;20; Caveat: Program description and policy framework; outcomes depend on country design and implementation.

title: Protection Gaps in Insurance for Natural Hazards and Retirement Savings in Asia
book_use: OECD describes parametric coverage, faster payout potential and basis-risk tradeoffs in natural-hazard protection gaps.; Chapter: 18;20; Caveat: Asia-focused report; examples do not imply identical market structure elsewhere.

title: The California Public Wildfire Model
book_use: California is developing a public wildfire catastrophe model intended to support insurance, mitigation, planning and public understanding of wildfire loss.; Chapter: 7;17;20; Caveat: Model is under development in 2026; it is not yet a validated operational pricing model.

title: Reform made real — forward-looking wildfire catastrophe model review
book_use: California completed review of a forward-looking wildfire catastrophe model and tied model/reinsurance use to commitments to expand writing in distressed areas.; Chapter: 7;8;20; Caveat: Department announcement describes intended regulatory effects; realized market outcomes require later evaluation.

title: Reports & Notices — Federal Insurance Office
book_use: Provides the underlying FIO homeowners-insurance analyses and other federal insurance research used for market context.; Chapter: 1;7; Caveat: Index page; claims should be traced to the linked underlying reports where material.

title: Climate change presses on: Devastating wildfires and intense thunderstorms exacerbate losses for insurers
book_use: Munich Re reported that no hurricane struck the U.S. mainland in 2025 while wildfire, severe thunderstorms and floods still drove major losses; its insured-loss total was about $107 billion.; Chapter: 7;10; Caveat: Industry loss estimates and peril classifications can differ from other catastrophe datasets; use as a second industry view rather than independent proof of attribution.

title: Lower losses, growing risks: the natural disaster review for the first half of 2026
book_use: Munich Re reported lower first-half 2026 natural-disaster losses than recent five-year averages while emphasizing that climate change and growing exposure continued to increase future loss risk.; Chapter: 7; Caveat: Half-year figures are preliminary and a quiet period is not evidence of a lower long-run loss distribution.

title: Business Blackout
book_use: Lloyd's modeled a severe but plausible cyber attack on the U.S. power grid in which insurance claims arose across more than 30 lines, illustrating cross-line accumulation.; Chapter: 12; Caveat: Scenario results are hypothetical stress-test outputs, not realized losses or forecasts; use only for accumulation logic.

title: Insuring AI: data centre value accumulation risks
book_use: Swiss Re describes AI data-centre projects with construction costs up to about $20 billion, dense physical and operational dependencies, and concentration across insureds and insurance lines.; Chapter: 21; Caveat: Forward-looking sector analysis with limited loss history for next-generation facilities; project costs and capacity forecasts can change.

title: Natural catastrophes: the USD 424bn protection gap and adaptation to counter growing exposure
book_use: Swiss Re estimates a 2025 modeled natural-catastrophe protection gap of $424 billion and reports a median projected benefit-cost ratio of 1.86 across reviewed adaptation projects.; Chapter: 18;20; Caveat: Protection-gap and benefit-cost figures are model- and project-set dependent; projected BCRs should not be treated as guaranteed realized returns.

title: What is an escrow or impound account?
book_use: Explains that mortgage servicers commonly use escrow to collect and pay property taxes and homeowners-insurance premiums, and that changing insurance costs can change the borrower's total monthly payment; also describes lender-obtained force-placed insurance when required coverage is not maintained.; Chapter: 1; Caveat: General consumer guidance and federal servicing context; individual loan contracts, escrow requirements and state insurance rules can differ.

title: McCarran-Ferguson Act
book_use: Explains the U.S. shift from Paul v. Virginia through South-Eastern Underwriters to the 1945 McCarran-Ferguson Act and the continuing primary role of states in regulating and taxing the business of insurance unless Congress provides otherwise.; Chapter: 17; Caveat: NAIC represents state insurance regulators and advocates for state-based regulation; use for historical and institutional orientation rather than neutral proof that the state model is superior.

title: Receivers' Handbook for Insurance Company Insolvencies — Chapter 7: Reinsurance
book_use: Defines treaty and facultative reinsurance and distinguishes proportional/pro rata from non-proportional/excess-of-loss structures, including quota-share and retention concepts used in Chapter 10.; Chapter: 10; Caveat: Technical regulatory handbook written for insolvency practice; contract structures vary and each treaty must be read on its own terms.

title: Insurance-Linked Securities
book_use: Explains catastrophe bonds as capital-market risk transfer, including principal-at-risk structures, common collateral solutions, trigger concepts and the role of cat bonds and sidecars in adding catastrophe capacity.; Chapter: 11; Caveat: NAIC overview incorporates market data and industry conventions; individual transactions can use different legal, collateral and trigger structures.

title: Risk-Based Capital
book_use: Explains risk-based capital as a statutory minimum tied to insurer size and operational/financial risk, used as an early-warning framework for progressively stronger regulatory intervention before insolvency.; Chapter: 5; Caveat: RBC is a regulatory threshold framework, not a complete solvency measure or a general ranking of insurer financial strength.

title: Guaranty Associations and Funds
book_use: Explains the role of state guaranty mechanisms in covered claims after insurer insolvency and their coordination with receivership and liquidation processes.; Chapter: 5; Caveat: Coverage is determined by state law and statutory limits; guaranty mechanisms are a safety net after failure, not a blanket federal guarantee or substitute for solvency supervision.
